title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
event_hint: arXiv publication of CodeGrep retrieval agent
problem: LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch, not patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified, a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, with many calls spent on grep, glob, and view_file during repository exploration.
mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B retrieval agent trained end-to-end with GRPO to issue multi-turn parallel grep/glob/read tool calls and return candidate files to a frozen downstream coding agent. It uses CATM (Code Agent Trajectory Mining) to mine supervision from 67K open-source agent trajectories, and a Git-worktree environment for multi-turn agent RL.

evidence.claim: CodeGrep v3 reduces resolved-instance rounds from 23.0 to 19.6 (-15%) and tokens from 631K to 514K (-19%) while improving resolve rate from 25.8% to 27.0% on SWE-Bench Verified
evidence.condition: on resolved SWE-Bench Verified instances, downstream agent: OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, temperature 0, 100-round max

evidence.claim: Retrieval quality follows a precision threshold: BM25 (precision 0.375) degrades downstream, Jina (0.445) is neutral, CodeGrep v3 (0.677) achieves net efficiency gains
evidence.condition: file-level precision on internal evaluation set, downstream utility threshold

evidence.claim: CodeGrep v3 achieves Fβ mean 0.576 (median 0.714) with precision 0.677 and recall 0.435, producing high-quality retrievals (Fβ≥0.8) on 43.0% of instances vs 7.0% for BM25/Jina
evidence.baseline: BM25: Fβ mean 0.359, Jina: Fβ mean 0.427
evidence.condition: internal evaluation set with CATM-mined labels, β=0.5 emphasizing precision over recall

evidence.claim: Reward design: applying efficiency signal at advantage layer (v2/v3) reduces KL drift to 0.09-0.15 vs 0.31 for reward layer (v1), with v3 stabilizing at 2.1 turns vs v1's 2.6
evidence.condition: GRPO training, KL-to-reference at step 900, mean turns per inference

evidence.claim: Training data from 67,074 open-source OpenHands trajectories using CATM pipeline, yielding 31,977 effective training samples (47.7% retention)

evaluation_context: SWE-Bench Verified (500 instances). Downstream agent: OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024) with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507. Temperature 0, 100-round maximum. Training: single 8x B200 node with LoRA, optimizer offload, and vLLM-colocated rollout. Early-stop at step 897 of planned 2000 steps. Internal evaluation set uses held-out SWE-Bench instances with CATM-mined labels audited by senior engineers.
limitations: Index construction cost, repository update overhead, and real-world deployment constraints not described in visible evidence. Precision-only evaluation (β=0.5) may mask recall trade-offs; explicit limitations section and comprehensive failure case analysis not visible in supplement. Whether precision threshold transfers to other downstream agents remains open (§7). v1's reward-layer scaling caused 3.4× higher KL drift and required 1.65× more inference turns than v3.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to agent acceleration. CodeGrep demonstrates a clean retrieval-based acceleration approach: training a smaller retrieval agent via RL to reduce redundant Read/Grep operations in larger coding agents. Key insights: (1) RL for tool policies works for code retrieval; (2) efficiency signal belongs at advantage layer, not reward layer; (3) retrievers need high precision (~0.68) to be net-positive for downstream agents; (4) Git-worktree environments enable practical multi-turn agent RL; (5) retrieval utility follows a precision threshold, not linear payoff. This validates precision-first retrieval acceleration without heavy indexing infrastructure.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the explicit limitations and failure cases discussed in the paper?
